version_note: MITRE ATLAS v2026.09 (ATLAS data collection modified-date 2026-09-15, release commit 3259f38 dated 2026-09-10; that release contains 1 matrix, 16 tactics, 120 techniques, 88 sub-techniques, 40 mitigations and 73 case studies). Source: official machine-readable dataset mitre-atlas/atlas-data, dist/v6/ATLAS-2026.09.yaml - https://github.com/mitre-atlas/atlas-data/blob/main/dist/v6/ATLAS-2026.09.yaml (the file that dist/v6/ATLAS-latest.yaml points to). Fetched from this sandbox via the GitHub contents API because raw.githubusercontent.com was unreachable; atlas.mitre.org is a JavaScript single-page app that returned only its shell (no data payload), so the official GitHub data file was used as the authoritative source. Sub-technique names use the framework's Parent Technique: Sub-technique form.

tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.description: The adversary gathers information about the AI system that can be used to plan future operations.

tactics.name: Resource Development
tactics.description: The adversary establishes resources, capabilities, and infrastructure to support AI-targeted operations.

tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.description: The adversary gains an initial foothold into the AI system or the environment it is connected to.

tactics.name: Execution
tactics.description: The adversary runs malicious instructions or code through AI artifacts, prompts, or agent tools.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.description: The adversary maintains a foothold by manipulating AI models, data, prompts, memory, or agent configuration.

tactics.name: Defense Evasion
tactics.description: The adversary avoids detection by AI guardrails, input filters, and AI-enabled security software.

tactics.name: Discovery
tactics.description: The adversary explores the AI environment to learn about models, prompts, data, tools, and agent capabilities.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.description: The adversary gathers AI artifacts and sensitive data reachable through AI services and their tools.

tactics.name: Exfiltration
tactics.description: The adversary steals AI artifacts, model internals, prompts, or data through AI channels.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: The adversary manipulates, degrades, or destroys AI systems, data, and confidence in their outputs.

tactics.name: Privilege Escalation
tactics.description: The adversary gains higher-level permissions through AI systems, agents, or their host environments.

tactics.name: Credential Access
tactics.description: The adversary steals credentials stored in, or reachable through, AI systems and agent tooling.

tactics.name: Command and Control
tactics.description: The adversary communicates with compromised AI systems in order to control them.

tactics.name: Lateral Movement
tactics.description: The adversary moves through the environment by abusing AI systems, agents, and their connected tools.

tactics.name: AI Model Access
tactics.description: The adversary obtains some level of access to an AI model, from inference API access to full model weights.

tactics.name: AI Attack Adaptation
tactics.description: The adversary adapts knowledge and capabilities into attack-ready payloads tailored to the target AI system.

techniques.name: Search Open AI Vulnerability Analysis
techniques.description: Searching public research, papers, and vulnerability write-ups for known attacks against the target AI model or system.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript shows the tester researching published attacks, CVEs, or papers about the target model family before attacking it.

techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Directly probing publicly reachable AI systems and endpoints to identify live, misconfigured, or vulnerable targets.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester runs network or port scanning, or queries internet-wide scan databases, to find reachable AI endpoints.

techniques.name: Active Scanning: Scan for Exposed AI Infrastructure
techniques.description: Scanning hosts and well-known ports to locate self-hosted AI runtimes, model-serving endpoints, and agent infrastructure.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript shows probing of default AI service ports or API paths such as /v1/models, Ollama 11434, or vLLM endpoints.

techniques.name: Discover AI Model Family
techniques.description: Fingerprinting which model or model family a system uses, in order to tailor later attacks.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester probes responses or metadata to determine the underlying model or vendor.

techniques.name: Evade AI Model
techniques.description: Crafting inputs or deepfakes that cause an AI model to misclassify or fail, evading AI-based detection or authentication.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester measures whether modified inputs slip past a classifier, filter, or biometric check, typically reporting a drop in detection rate.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities: Adversarial AI Attack Implementations
techniques.description: Obtaining or reusing open-source implementations of AI attacks such as adversarial-example or LLM testing frameworks.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript shows the tester installing or invoking a known adversarial-AI or LLM red-team library instead of hand-crafting the attack.

techniques.name: Training Data Poisoning
techniques.description: Manipulating training or fine-tuning data to bias, degrade, or backdoor the resulting model.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester injects or proposes poisoned samples into a training or fine-tuning corpus and measures the resulting behavior shift.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via AI Inference API: Infer Training Data Membership
techniques.description: Inferring whether specific samples were present in a model's training data, leaking privacy-sensitive membership information.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester measures confidence or loss differences to decide whether a specific record was part of the training data.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via AI Inference API: Invert AI Model
techniques.description: Reconstructing training data by strategically querying the confidence scores exposed by an inference API.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester queries the API repeatedly in order to reconstruct features or samples from the training data.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via AI Inference API: Extract AI Model
techniques.description: Querying a model to build a dataset and train a functional clone that mimics the victim's model.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester harvests input and output pairs at scale with the stated goal of training a copy of the model.

techniques.name: Denial of AI Service
techniques.description: Flooding or overloading an AI service with requests or expensive inputs in order to degrade or shut it down.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester sends high volumes or computationally expensive prompts to exhaust the service.

techniques.name: Cost Harvesting
techniques.description: Driving up the victim's AI service costs through high-volume or high-complexity queries and agent activity.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester's goal is financial: maximizing tokens, tool calls, or agent iterations to inflate the victim's bill.

techniques.name: Craft Adversarial Data: White-Box Optimization
techniques.description: Optimizing adversarial inputs directly against a fully known target model for maximum effect.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester has model weights or gradients and optimizes a perturbation directly against them.

techniques.name: Craft Adversarial Data: Black-Box Optimization
techniques.description: Optimizing adversarial inputs through repeated queries to a model that is only reachable via an API.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester iteratively queries the API, tracking a query budget, to evolve an adversarial input.

techniques.name: Craft Adversarial Data: Insert Backdoor Trigger
techniques.description: Adding a specific trigger pattern to inputs that activates a backdoor previously implanted in a model.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester checks whether a rare trigger token or pattern flips the model to attacker-controlled output.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Injection
techniques.description: Crafting malicious prompts that make an LLM disregard its original instructions and follow the adversary's instructions instead.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript contains instructions telling the model to disregard prior instructions or to adopt an attacker-supplied role.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Injection: Direct
techniques.description: Injecting malicious prompts directly as a user of the LLM in order to hijack or misuse the model.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester types the injection payload directly into the chat as the user's own message.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Injection: Indirect
techniques.description: Injecting prompts indirectly through documents, emails, websites, or other data the LLM or agent ingests.
techniques.detect_hints: The payload arrives inside retrieved or fetched content rather than from the user, and the model then acts on it.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Injection: Triggered
techniques.description: Triggering a previously planted prompt injection through a specific user action or event in the environment.
techniques.detect_hints: Injected instructions lie dormant until a defined keyword, event, or later conversation turn activates them.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tool Invocation
techniques.description: Using access to an AI agent to invoke its connected tools, extending the adversary's reach and privileges.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript shows the agent being steered into calling a tool such as email, shell, database, or file access.

techniques.name: LLM Jailbreak
techniques.description: Inducing an LLM to ignore or override its safety alignment and guardrails in order to produce withheld outputs.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester uses personas, fictional framing, or refusal-suppression prompts to obtain content the model would normally refuse.

techniques.name: Extract LLM System Prompt
techniques.description: Extracting an LLM system prompt through prompt injection or from configuration files.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester works to obtain the exact system prompt text, often as a headline finding.

techniques.name: LLM Data Leakage
techniques.description: Crafting prompts that induce an LLM to reveal private user data, proprietary training data, or other users' information.
techniques.detect_hints: The model returns secrets, personal data, or another tenant's content in response to the tester's prompts.

techniques.name: Discover LLM Hallucinations
techniques.description: Prompting the model to surface hallucinated packages, URLs, or entities that can later be registered or published.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester collects fabricated package names, domains, or references the model invents, as future attack targets.

techniques.name: Gather RAG-Indexed Targets
techniques.description: Identifying the external data sources indexed by a retrieval-augmented generation system in order to target them.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester enumerates or reasons about the documents, vector store, or knowledge base that the RAG pipeline retrieves from.

techniques.name: LLM Prompt Obfuscation
techniques.description: Hiding or encoding prompts so that humans, guardrails, or detection mechanisms fail to notice them.
techniques.detect_hints: The payload is encoded, split, or rendered invisibly so filters and human reviewers miss it while the model still parses it.

techniques.name: Discover LLM System Information: System Prompt
techniques.description: Learning the system instructions given to an LLM in order to understand its capabilities and circumvent its guardrails.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester asks the model to disclose, repeat, or paraphrase the instructions it was configured with.

techniques.name: RAG Poisoning
techniques.description: Injecting malicious content into a retrieval index so it surfaces in future RAG search results and alters model behavior.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester plants crafted documents in the retrieval corpus and confirms the assistant later cites or obeys them.

techniques.name: LLM Response Rendering
techniques.description: Inducing the LLM to emit markdown or HTML that makes the victim's client fetch an attacker-controlled URL, exfiltrating data.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript shows private data encoded into an image URL, link, or HTML fragment that the client will render.

techniques.name: AI Agent Context Poisoning
techniques.description: Manipulating an AI agent's LLM context, memory, or thread so that its behavior changes persistently.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester gets the agent to store an instruction in memory, or relies on earlier turns to keep influencing later ones.

techniques.name: Credentials from AI Agent Configuration
techniques.description: Reading API keys, tokens, and connection strings stored in an AI agent's configuration.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester finds credentials in agent configuration files, environment variables, or tool settings.

techniques.name: Discover AI Agent Configuration
techniques.description: Discovering an AI agent's configuration, including the tools and services it can reach.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester asks the agent what tools it has access to, or reads its configuration file or dashboard.

techniques.name: Data from AI Services
techniques.description: Collecting proprietary or sensitive data through an organization's AI services, RAG stores, and agent tools.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester pulls internal documents or records through the assistant that a normal user could not reach directly.

techniques.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
techniques.description: Using an agent's write-capable tools to send sensitive data to an attacker-controlled destination.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester encodes stolen data into the parameters of a legitimate write tool such as email, docs, or CRM.

techniques.name: Manipulate User LLM Chat History
techniques.description: Editing or deleting a user's LLM chat history to conceal the adversary's changes or probing.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester modifies, deletes, or rewrites prior chat turns to cover tracks or hide an injected instruction.

techniques.name: Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Placing malicious prompts into a public-facing application so the victim's system ingests them later through RAG, agents, or user interaction.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester writes prompt payloads into a public web surface such as a review, comment, profile, or support ticket, expecting the AI to read them later.

techniques.name: Delay Execution of LLM Instructions
techniques.description: Planting instructions that execute only on a future event or turn in order to slip past per-turn controls.
techniques.detect_hints: The injected instruction explicitly waits for a later trigger or conversation turn before taking effect.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting
techniques.description: Using agent tools to harvest credentials from document stores, code repositories, and productivity systems.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester uses the agent's connected tools to search mail, drives, repositories, or notes for secrets.

techniques.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation
techniques.description: Invoking an agent's mutative tools in order to delete or destroy data and files.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester drives the agent into destructive file, database, or record operations.

techniques.name: Escape to Host
techniques.description: Breaking out of a container or sandbox around an AI system in order to reach the underlying host.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester tries to break out of the sandbox or container that hosts the model or agent execution environment.

techniques.name: AI Agent Tool Poisoning
techniques.description: Poisoning an agent tool's definition, implementation, or runtime responses so the agent behaves differently from what the tool represents.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript describes a modified tool description, package, or MCP server that misleads the agent while appearing benign.

techniques.name: Triggers in Multimodal Inputs
techniques.description: Embedding instructions or triggers in a non-text modality so that controls that only inspect text miss them.
techniques.detect_hints: The payload rides inside an image, audio clip, or document rendering while the text channel looks clean.

techniques.name: AI Agent Response Biasing
techniques.description: Injecting instructions that bias an assistant toward adversary-chosen sources or recommendations in its answers.
techniques.detect_hints: The payload instructs the assistant to favor, promote, or always cite a chosen source in its responses.

techniques.name: Crafted AI Assistant Links
techniques.description: Crafting URLs that pre-populate or auto-submit an attacker-chosen prompt when an AI assistant link is opened.
techniques.detect_hints: The transcript contains assistant URLs carrying a prompt or query parameter that feeds the tester's payload straight into the chat.

techniques.name: Misconfigured or Publicly Exposed AI Services
techniques.description: Exploiting AI services with missing authentication or overly permissive access controls to reach agents and LLM runtimes.
techniques.detect_hints: The tester reaches an LLM or agent endpoint without credentials, or notes absent or default authentication as the way in.
